version_notes: Original Wacky Insights art direction informed by professional explainer-animation principles: clear vector characters, rich reusable environments, integrated educational graphics, purposeful motion, and distinct seamless scene transitions.

channel_personality.target_viewer_reaction: I actually learned something — and that was funny.

visual_identity.readability_goal: The main idea and focal subject should be readable in under one second.
visual_identity.reference_translation_rule: Borrow only broad explainer-animation principles such as clarity, modularity, environment variety and integrated information graphics. Never copy another channel's characters, branding, exact compositions, assets or proprietary visual identity.

environments.rule: Most shots should feel like a real place with story context rather than floating objects on an empty background. Build a diverse reusable environment library so consecutive scenes can genuinely change location when the story calls for it.

educational_visuals.rule: Whenever possible, explain the mechanism inside the active world instead of replacing the world with a full-screen information board.

humour_visuals.rule: Visual jokes should improve memorability, pacing or relatability without making the educational mechanism unclear.

palette_rules: Backgrounds should usually be slightly muted so the active subject reads first.
Use no more than two or three strong accent colours in one shot where practical.
Keep infographic emphasis colours consistent within a scene.

text.purpose: Text should label, compare, clarify or punch up action. It must not carry the whole explanation.

scene_balance.note: Ratios are directional. Default to active environments with characters and props; integrate infographics into those scenes.

scene_transition_rules.goal: Transitions must feel seamless but clearly intentional. The viewer should feel progression, never an accidental blink.
scene_transition_rules.core_rule: A true scene change should introduce a meaningfully different shot. If the next shot has nearly the same environment, framing and focal action, keep it within the same scene and use a reframe, camera move, insert, reaction shot, overlay beat or prop state change instead.

shot_variety.rule: Do not repeatedly show the same character in the same location at the same scale. Reused environments must be meaningfully reframed or continued as one scene.

forbidden: flat empty backgrounds without story context
decorative motion that adds no story explanation humour or emphasis
long static charts disconnected from the environment
hard cuts between nearly identical shots
